backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 linearly up to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param-group before the update. No other changes.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Change the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside the Muon update from its current value to 4 (or 6 if 5 is current) and keep the quintic coefficients unchanged. This trades orthogonalization accuracy against per-step time in the fixed 300 s budget. Only the iteration loop bound changes.
backlog.title: Newton-Schulz iteration count for Muon

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon learning rate for each transformer block by a factor (1 - 0.5*layer_idx/(DEPTH-1)), so the first block gets the full MATRIX_LR and the last block gets half. Apply this multiplier when building the Muon parameter groups, grouping matrices by their layer index. Leave embeddings and scalars unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-depth Muon LR decay

backlog.spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.1 for the per-layer residual and skip-mixing scalars while keeping every other Adam group unchanged. Put these scalars in their own Adam param group with the new LR. Everything else in the optimizer setup stays the same.
backlog.title: Lower scalar LR for residual lambdas

backlog.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and set the beta1 of the embedding Adam group to 0.9 while the other Adam groups keep ADAM_BETAS. Only the embedding param group's hyperparameters change. This tests whether the very high embedding LR is overshooting early in training.
backlog.title: Embedding LR and beta tuning

backlog.spec: Add global gradient-norm clipping with max norm 1.0 applied after backward and before the optimizer step, across all parameters. Use torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ on model parameters. Leave the optimizer and schedules untouched.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping on global norm

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget instead of 50%, keeping the warmdown shape unchanged. Only the constant is modified. This tests whether a longer anneal improves the final val_bpb within 300 s.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio increase

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 to its peak over the first 2% of the time budget before the existing warmdown begins. Do not change the warmdown logic. This guards against early instability from the high embedding and scalar LRs.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to 0.1x peak over the warmdown window, keeping WARMDOWN_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC as they are. Compute the multiplier from elapsed time fraction. Apply the same multiplier to all optimizer groups.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown with floor

backlog.spec: Replace the warmdown multiplier with sqrt-shaped decay: multiplier = sqrt(max(0, remaining_fraction)), where remaining_fraction goes from 1 to 0 across the warmdown window. Keep the constant-LR phase before warmdown unchanged. Apply uniformly to every param group.
backlog.title: Sqrt-decay warmdown

backlog.spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 and keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64, so gradient accumulation steps are halved accordingly. This doubles the number of optimizer steps in 300 s at the cost of noisier gradients. Keep all LRs unchanged.
backlog.title: Batch size halving

backlog.spec: Start at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17 and double it at fixed time fractions (e.g. at 25% and 50% of the budget) until it reaches 2**19, adjusting gradient accumulation steps each time. Keep the LR schedule keyed to elapsed time. Only the accumulation count and the batch target change over time.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp

backlog.spec: Train with a shorter context early: use sequence length 512 for the first 40% of the time budget and the full context length for the rest, adjusting the batch shape so the token count per step stays fixed. Keep the sliding-window pattern consistent with the reduced length. This raises early step throughput.
backlog.title: Sequence length curriculum

backlog.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits as logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy loss, in the forward pass used for training and evaluation. Keep the same loss function and reduction. This bounds logit magnitude and stabilizes the high LR training.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Apply RMS normalization to query and key vectors per head after the rotary embedding is applied and before the attention dot product. Use no learned gain or a fixed unit gain. Keep the attention scale factor at 1/sqrt(head_dim).
backlog.title: QK normalization

backlog.spec: Compute the value projection of the first block once and add a learned per-layer scalar-weighted mix of that first-layer value into the value of every later attention layer. Initialize the mixing scalars so the first-layer contribution starts at 0. Keep all other attention computation unchanged.
backlog.title: Value residual from first layer

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation with squared ReLU, computing relu(x) squared after the up projection and before the down projection. Keep the MLP hidden width the same. Only the activation function changes.
backlog.title: Squared ReLU MLP activation

backlog.spec: Change the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 to extend the effective positional wavelength for the sliding-window and full-attention layers. Keep the head dimension and the rotation implementation unchanged. Only the base constant changes.
backlog.title: RoPE base frequency

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSSSL' or 'SSLL' (choose the one that keeps the final layer full-context) and keep all other attention settings the same. This tests the local/global attention mix under the fixed time budget. Only the pattern string changes.
backlog.title: Window pattern change

backlog.spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 while keeping model_dim approximately fixed by reducing ASPECT_RATIO so that depth times ASPECT_RATIO stays close to the current width, rounded so HEAD_DIM still divides model_dim. Keep all other settings unchanged. This tests depth versus throughput under a 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Deeper and narrower model

backlog.spec: Decrease DEPTH from 8 to 6 and increase ASPECT_RATIO so model_dim grows by roughly 1.33x, keeping HEAD_DIM dividing model_dim. Keep all other settings unchanged. This gives more steps per second in the fixed time budget with a wider model.
backlog.title: Shallower and wider model

backlog.spec: Tie the lm_head weight to the token embedding weight so both share one parameter, and remove the separate UNEMBEDDING_LR Adam group by folding the shared parameter into the embedding group. Scale the output by 1/sqrt(model_dim) before the head projection to balance magnitudes. Keep the rest of the model identical.
backlog.title: Tied embedding and unembedding

backlog.spec: Initialize the lm_head weight with std 0.001 (or zero) instead of its current init, so initial predictions are uniform and training starts from a clean baseline. Keep the embedding init and all other layers unchanged. Only the initialization of the head changes.
backlog.title: Zero-init or small-init lm_head

backlog.spec: Add one learnable scalar per attention head that multiplies the attention logits, initialized so the effective scale equals the standard 1/sqrt(head_dim). Place this scalar in the scalar Adam group. Keep the rest of the attention path unchanged.
backlog.title: Learnable attention temperature

backlog.spec: Add a second token-embedding table indexed by a hash of the previous token and the current token (modulo a bucket count of about 4096), with dimension equal to model_dim and zero init. Add its output to the standard token embedding before the first block. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Bigram hash embedding

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss of 1e-4 times the mean squared log-sum-exp of the logits over all positions, computed from the same logits used for cross-entropy. Add it to the training loss only, not the evaluation path. This stabilizes logit scale without changing the main objective.
backlog.title: Z-loss regularizer

backlog.spec: Keep WEIGHT_DECAY at 0.2 for the first half of training and linearly decay it to 0.0 by the end of the time budget for the Muon parameter groups. Update the value each step from elapsed time. Adam groups keep their current settings.
backlog.title: Muon weight decay schedule

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step, and use the EMA weights for the final evaluation call. Keep the training forward pass on the live weights. Do not change the evaluation function itself, only which weights are loaded into the model before it is called.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for evaluation

backlog.spec: Build training sequences by packing consecutive documents with a BOS separator and mask attention or loss so tokens do not attend across document boundaries where the data loader exposes boundaries. Keep the token count per step the same. This removes wasted padding tokens from the training stream.
backlog.title: Padding-free document packing

backlog.spec: Change the torch.compile call on the model to use mode='max-autotune' (or 'reduce-overhead' if compile time is an issue) so the fused kernels run faster within the fixed time budget. Keep the eager fallback path unchanged. Only the compile options change.
backlog.title: Torch compile mode for throughput

backlog.spec: Add a second token-embedding table (same vocab, model_dim width) and, for each layer, mix it into the attention values: v = v + lambda_l * value_embed(idx), where lambda_l is a new per-layer scalar initialized to 0 and trained with the scalar Adam group at SCALAR_LR. Compute value_embed(idx) once per forward pass from the input token ids and reuse it in every layer. Leave the attention score computation, sliding-window pattern and lm_head unchanged. This gives deep layers a direct route to token identity without passing through the residual stream.
backlog.title: Value embeddings mixed into attention values

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block from the sequential form x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x)) to the parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), sharing one RMSNorm per block for both branches. Keep the per-layer residual scalars, QK normalization, sliding-window pattern and all learning rates unchanged. The parallel form removes one serial dependency per layer, which may allow the same quality with less wall-clock per step inside the fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP residual blocks

backlog.spec: After scaled-dot-product attention and before the output projection, multiply each head's output by a learned sigmoid gate computed from the block input: g = sigmoid(W_g x) with W_g a small linear layer from model_dim to n_head, initialized so that the gate starts near 1 (zero weight, bias +3). Apply it element-wise per head, then run the existing output projection. Train W_g with the Muon matrix group like other projections. This lets each layer suppress uninformative heads and is a small architectural change with little extra compute.
backlog.title: Per-head sigmoid output gate on attention

backlog.spec: Take the hidden state after the middle layer (layer index DEPTH//2), apply the final norm and the shared lm_head to get auxiliary logits, and add its cross-entropy to the main loss with weight 0.3 during training only. The main output is unchanged and evaluation uses only the final layer. The auxiliary gradient gives the lower half of the network a direct training signal, which may speed up early learning in a short run. Linearly decay the auxiliary weight to 0 over the last 50% of the time budget so the final model is optimised for the main loss alone.
backlog.title: Deep supervision with an auxiliary early-exit loss

backlog.spec: Add one extra linear head (model_dim to vocab, sharing no weights with lm_head) that predicts the token two positions ahead from the final hidden state. Its cross-entropy, computed on positions with a valid t+2 target, is added to the main next-token loss with weight 0.2. Only the next-token head is used at evaluation, so the reported metric is unchanged in definition. Initialize the extra head at zero to avoid perturbing early training. This is a bold change to the training objective that may improve the representation per optimizer step.
backlog.title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam optimizer used for the embedding, lm_head and scalar parameter groups with a schedule-free AdamW variant: keep a fast iterate z updated by Adam, and an averaged iterate x used for the forward pass and final evaluation, with interpolation coefficient 0.9 and no learning-rate warmdown for these groups. Keep the Muon matrix group and its existing LR schedule unchanged. This removes the need for the warmdown on the Adam groups, so the schedule tuning done so far applies only to Muon. Keep the existing learning rates as the base step sizes.
backlog.title: Schedule-free AdamW for non-matrix parameters

backlog.spec: Since TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE was halved from 2^19 to 2^18, scale the learning rates of the Adam groups and the Muon group by the square root of the batch ratio relative to the original 2^19 batch, i.e. multiply each LR by sqrt(2^18 / 2^19) = 0.7071 for the Adam groups only, and keep MATRIX_LR at its current value as a control. Implement this as a single derived constant applied when building the param groups, so the change is one line of logic. The goal is to test whether the Adam side was over-stepped after the batch change, while the Muon side is left alone.
backlog.title: Batch-size-scaled Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: During training only, drop each block's attention branch and MLP branch independently with a per-layer keep probability that decreases linearly with depth, from 1.0 at layer 0 to 0.9 at the last layer. When a branch is dropped, its output is zeroed for that sample; kept branches are scaled by 1/keep_prob so expected activations match. Disable all dropping at evaluation time. This is a regularizer that makes the deeper layers less co-adapted, and it costs almost no compute per step.
backlog.title: Stochastic depth on residual branches

backlog.spec: Add decoupled weight decay with coefficient 0.01 (scaled by the group learning rate, AdamW-style) to the embedding, lm_head and scalar parameter groups, which currently have no weight decay. Leave the Muon group's cautious weight decay of WEIGHT_DECAY unchanged. Use the same decay for the embedding and lm_head groups and exclude the per-layer scalars from it. This regularises the large embedding table, which is the most overparameterised part of the model relative to the number of tokens seen in 300 s.
backlog.title: Adam-group weight decay on embeddings and scalars

backlog.spec: At initialization, scale the output projection of every attention block and every MLP block by 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH), so the variance added to the residual stream by each block is bounded as depth grows. Keep the input embedding scale and all other initializations unchanged. Do not change the per-layer residual scalars or the learning rates. This is a small, zero-cost change to the init that stabilises the residual stream at the current depth of 8 and may allow a higher effective step size early in the run.
backlog.title: Depth-scaled residual initialization

cand.description: Replace linear warmdown with a schedule-free AdamW variant for non-matrix parameters

incumbent.description: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to increase optimizer step frequency at the cost of gradient noise, which often helps convergence on small models under tight time budgets.

memo: Helped: halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (slot 7) is the only accepted change, official 1.0924, delta -0.0221. More optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s look like the main lever. Did not help: schedule shapes (cosine to 0.1x was +0.0517; sqrt decay -0.0003), tying lm_head to wte (+0.0079), lower embedding LR (+0.0011), and model shape changes (depth 6 +0.0082, depth 10 +0.0293). Small gains that were rejected: gradient clipping (-0.0032), sequence curriculum (-0.0048 over 2 runs), and removing the EMA block (-0.0013, 1.0911). Those were measured against the old incumbent, so they may be worth stacking on the new one. Next: halve the batch size again and retune LR to match. Retry the batch ramp-up with exact SEARCH blocks. Then test clipping and the curriculum on the new incumbent, with replicates to separate noise. Skip further schedule-shape and model-size experiments.
